title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student tells the makerspace assistant, "I am allergic to acrylic dust." On Wednesday the same student opens a new chat session. The team stored nothing from Monday. What does the model know about the allergy on Wednesday?

options.text: It knows, because the model keeps every chat it has had
It knows, because the context window is large enough
It knows nothing, because the program did not send it
It knows a little, because the system prompt kept it

items.stem: One request uses 3 model calls. The start of the context (rules, tool descriptions and question) is 400 tokens. Each tool result is 600 tokens. Call 1 has no tool result, call 2 follows one tool result, and call 3 follows two. Ignore the model's own output. How many tokens does the model read in total over all 3 calls?

The assistant must answer questions from 30 machine manuals, about 6,000 pages in all. A teammate proposes to paste all 30 manuals into the context for every question, because the model's window is big enough. What is the strongest objection?

options.text: Every call would pay for every page, and the model may use it badly
A model cannot read text that a person wrote for other people
The manuals would be lost at the end of each request
A large context makes the model refuse to call any tools

items.stem: In a retrieval system for the manuals, the model answers "the manual does not say" about a setting that is printed in the manual. In one sentence, what is the first thing to check, and why?
Your team wants the assistant to know that a student passed 3D-printer safety training. In one or two sentences, say where to store this fact, and why an agent-written note is a poor choice for it.
